profile.constituencyprofile_Text: The Jaggayyapeta Assembly Constituency Vision Action Plan 2024–29 is designed to leverage the region’s strengths in agriculture, industry, construction, and services, while aligning with Swarna Andhra @ 2047 and Viksit Bharat @ 2047. Geographically, the constituency lies in N.T.R. District, comprising three mandals—Jaggayyapeta, Vatsavai, Penuganchiprolu—and part of Nandigama Mandal (10 villages). It also includes Jaggayyapeta Municipality, which serves as the headquarters. Historically, the region holds immense cultural significance. The ancient Buddhist stupa remains at Dhanam Bodu, dating back over 2,000 years, reflect its heritage. Declared a municipality in 1987, Jaggayyapeta also houses important religious landmarks. Chief among them is the Sri Lakshmi Thirupatamma Ammvari Temple in Penuganchiprolu, the second-largest temple in N.T.R. District and the eighth-largest in Andhra Pradesh. Other notable temples include Tirumalagiri, Vedadri, Mukteswarapuram, and Damuluru, attracting thousands of devotees. Economically, the region thrives on agriculture and horticulture, supported by strong connectivity to Vijayawada, Kodad, and Khammam (Telangana), making it a strategic hub for trade, logistics, and industrial expansion. The Vision Plan targets a 15% annual growth rate by focusing on sustainable development, cultural preservation, and economic modernization, transforming Jaggayyapeta into a model constituency contributing to Andhra Pradesh’s and India’s long-term growth goals.
profile.geography: The Jaggayyapeta Assembly Constituency, spanning 697 sq. km with 73 villages and 66 grama panchayats, lies in the erstwhile Krishna district, bordered by Nandigama and Pedakurapadu Constituencies. Fertile red and black soils support paddy, chilli, cotton, and subabul, with 66% land under cultivation, 28% non-cultivable, and 6% forest. The Nagarjuna Sagar Canal, rivers Krishna, Paleru, and Munneru, and canals ensure strong irrigation, boosting paddy farming and aquaculture.
profile.populationDesc: Jaggayyapeta has a total population of 2,59,210 in that 2,05,680 (79%) residing in rural areas and 53,530 (21%) in urban areas. The constituency has 69,459 households with a sex ratio of 1009 females per 1,000 males with population density of 395 per square kilometers.
profile.administrationDesc: Jaggayyapeta Constituency is one of the seven assembly constituencies in NTR District. It has Jaggayyapeta, Vatsavai, Penuganchiprolu and Part of Nandigama Mandals.
profile.educationHealthcareDesc:
In addition to human healthcare, the constituency has a strong veterinary network, comprising 2 veterinary hospitals and 10 veterinary dispensaries, which play a crucial role in supporting the health of livestock and domestic animals—an important aspect of the rural economy.

Jaggayyapeta offers a strong education network with 76 primary, 40 upper primary, and 53 high schools, along with junior, degree, ITI, and engineering colleges. Welfare hostels support marginalized students. Healthcare is served by 2 Community Health Centers, 3 Primary Health Centers and 37 sub-centers, plus ensuring accessible education and medical care for all.
profile.culturalheritageDesc: Sri Lakshmi Tirupatamma Ammavari Temple in Penuganchiprolu, the Sri Bhavani Mukteswara Swamy Temple in Mukteswarapuram, and the Buddhist Stupa at Dhanam Bodu, Venkateswara Swamy (Tirumala Giri), Yogananda Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy (Vedadri), Koti Lingala Kshetram (Mukteswarapuram), and Sangameswara Swamy (Damuluru)

economy_text.economy_Text: Jaggayyapeta presents a comprehensive growth strategy to transform the constituency into an economically vibrant, investment-friendly, and employment-driven region. With a Gross Constituency Domestic Product (GCDP) of ₹9,713 crores in 2023-24 (FRE), Jaggayyapeta is projected to achieve₹1,96,888 crores by 2047-48, reflecting a strong and sustainable annual growth trajectory averaging 12-15%. As of 2023-24, the economy is led by the service sector, contributing 47.15% to the Gross Value Added (GVA), followed by the industrial sector at 29%, and the agriculture and allied sector at 23.85%.
economy_text.gcdP_Growth_Text: Jaggayyapeta is witnessing steady economic momentum with a targeted 12 - 15% annual GCDP growth rate across key sectors like Construction, Horticulture, and Transport. This growth trajectory aligns with the long-term vision of making the constituency a vibrant economic hub by 2047.
